problems.claim: WSLC: whether a container can reach a host service is 'not documented'.
problems.problem: Overstated. wslc-state-aware.md says allowing ingress/host-loopback 'does not create host port forwarding or promise reachability across NAT', and 'a host loopback listener is not made guest-reachable by spelling its host address localhost'. The getting-started doc says an external proxy 'must have an address routable from the container'. So the docs do speak to this: loopback is not reachable, and a host-routable address is the only route. The study should have quoted these and not left it as unknown. The only truly untested part is whether a host-routable address plus a host firewall rule works. It would also require all-allow (unrestricted, bridged) egress for the coder, which defeats the confinement goal.
problems.evidence: v1.0.0 wslc-state-aware.md lines 143-145 and 179-181; wsl-container-getting-started.md lines 358 and 392-396.
